Title: Foreign man arrested over alleged assault, intimidation of student
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have arrested a foreign man suspected of assaulting and criminally intimidating a local student at a residential area in Sungai Besi.
Cheras police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Rosdi Daud said the suspect, a 39-year-old man who works as a composer, was detained during a raid at a condominium unit here at about 1.51am on July 26.
"Based on our checks, the incident occurred on July 11 involving a local student from a private institution in his 30s," he said.
He said the arrest was carried out by a team from the Cheras police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Department (D7), acting on intelligence.
"The suspect is being investigated under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt and Section 506 of the Penal Code for criminal intimidation.
"He has been remanded until Aug 10, while the investigation paper is being finalised before being referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor for further action," he said in a statement today.
Rosdi did not disclose further details regarding the alleged assault or the circumstances that led to the incident.

Title: Ringgit eases versus US dollar, ends higher against other major currencies
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended lower against the US dollar although it strengthened versus other major currencies on Tuesday, as the greenback remained supported by stronger-than-expected US manufacturing data.
At 6pm, the local currency eased against the greenback to 4.0945/0985 from Monday's close of 4.0935/0975.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US dollar is likely to remain well supported as positive economic data from the United States reinforces confidence in the strength of the US economy.
"The US Dollar Index (DXY) surpassed the 100-point mark again after the US Institute for Supply Management Manufacturing Index for July came in better than expected," he told Bernama.
Nevertheless, Mohd Afzanizam said, the ringgit was mostly flat versus the US dollar and moved within a narrow range throughout the day.
The ringgit traded higher against a basket of major currencies at the close.
It appreciated versus the Japanese yen to 2.5929/5956 from 2.6062/6089 at Monday's close, strengthened vis-à-vis the euro to 4.7120/7166 from 4.7165/7211 yesterday, and edged up against the British pound to 5.5034/5088 from 5.5053/5107 previously.
The ringgit also traded higher against regional currencies.
It strengthened versus the Thai baht to 12.2487/2654 from 12.2663/2827 at yesterday's close, rose against the Indonesian rupiah to 227.1/227.4 from 227.4/227.7 previously, appreciated vis-à-vis the Philippine peso to 6.69/6.70 from 6.72/6.73, and advanced against the Singapore dollar to 3.1899/1932 from 3.1911/1944.

Title: LTAT stresses prudent management of military personnel savings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT) has reaffirmed its commitment to safeguarding the savings of about 117,000 military personnel and delivering sustainable long-term returns.
Its chief executive Mohammad Ashraf Md Radzi said LTAT bore a significant responsibility as the contributions entrusted to it belonged to armed forces personnel who had devoted the prime years of their lives to serving the country.
"LTAT is unique because the savings we manage belong to armed forces personnel who have dedicated their lives and prime years to the nation.
"These contributions represent a major responsibility, and we have managed that trust well, particularly by delivering consistent and sustainable dividends," he said after a corporate visit to Media Prima Berhad at Balai Berita Bangsar here today.
Ashraf said LTAT would continue managing its members' contributions prudently while strengthening efforts to provide sustainable returns.
He said the fund had about 117,000 contributors, comprising armed forces officers and personnel of other ranks, who have been required to contribute since 2016.
He added that LTAT savings provided personnel with a financial safety net after they completed their military service.
Many personnel served for up to 26 years and left the armed forces while still in their 40s, he said.
"At that age, they still have family responsibilities and need a source of income to continue supporting themselves and their families.
"LTAT provides them with a financial safety net upon completing their careers in the Armed Forces."
On the corporate visit, Ashraf said cooperation with the media was important in communicating LTAT's activities, achievements and initiatives to armed forces personnel and other stakeholders.
"Media Prima is one of the best platforms for us to communicate the positive work being carried out by LTAT in fulfilling the responsibility entrusted to us," he said.
The LTAT delegation was welcomed by Media Prima group managing director Datuk Rafiq Razali before being taken on a tour of Media Prima Audio, the News and Current Affairs studios, Rev Media Group and Klik, the New Straits Times Press archive facility on the editorial floor.
The delegation was received on the editorial floor by Media Prima deputy group managing editor and New Straits Times group editor Farrah Naz Karim.
The visit also included a corporate presentation by Rafiq and a question-and-answer session between the senior management teams of LTAT and Media Prima.
Also present from Media Prima were Media Prima Content, TV Networks and Primeworks Studios chief executive officer Nini Yusof; Media Prima Audio chief executive officer Nazri Noran; Media Prima Omnia chief operating officer (Direct Solutions) Datuk Mohd Efendi Omar; and Big Tree chief operating officer Muhamad Fariz Mustafa.
They were joined by Media Prima News and Current Affairs group managing editor Jasbant Singh and Media Prima group general manager for the Group Chairman's Office and Group Corporate Communications Azlan Abdul Aziz.
The LTAT delegation included its chief investment officer Ahmad Farouk Mohamed; senior director and risk management and compliance head Azleen Ismail; director and strategic communications head Mohammad Izzat Abdul Aziz Alhadjri; and strategic planning head Jasmaliha Jaafar.
Also present were investment strategy and asset allocation head Sulaiman Mohamed Ridza; finance head Syazrin Eliza Yazid; member services head Khairul Anwar Ismail; and assistant vice-president in the chief executive's office Muzakkir Muhammad Diah.
They were joined by strategic communications assistant vice-president Muhammad Aliff Nazrin; senior associate Zunafishailmy Mohd Napis; and MySTEP officer with the Strategic Communications Department Aidil Yusrif.

Title: Employers under probe after 49 workers checked in Pangkor op
Article:
IPOH: A total of four fishing premises were inspected involving 49 workers, comprising 44 foreigners from Thailand, Cambodia, Laos and Indonesia, as well as five local workers during the Integrated Anti-Human Trafficking Enforcement Operation, off the waters of Pulau Pangkor yesterday.
Perak Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) director Maritime Captain Mohamad Shukri Khotob said in a statement today that the operation was carried out in collaboration with the Perak Labour Department, involving 37 personnel from both agencies.
"The inspection found that several employers are suspected of committing various labour law violations, including failing to notify the Labour Office of the hiring of foreign workers within 14 days from the date of hiring as stipulated under the Employment Act 1955," he said.
[[nid:1504140]]
In addition, he said the inspection also found that there were employers who paid wages in cash without providing employment contracts and pay slips, paying wages below the minimum wage rate set under the National Wages Consultative Council Act 2011.
He said there are also employers who failed to obtain the Certificate of Accommodation from the Labour Department as required under the Employees Minimum Standards of Housing, Accommodation and Employee Amenities Act 1990.
Shukri said that all the employers involved are being investigated and further action will be taken by the Perak Labour Department in accordance with the applicable legal provisions.
He said the integrated operations focused on inspecting fishing premises to ensure compliance with labour laws, detecting elements of human trafficking, and combating labour exploitation, particularly involving foreign workers.
[[nid:1504139]]
The integrated operations was part of the government's ongoing efforts to strengthen cross-agency enforcement to ensure the welfare of workers is continuously protected, while also combating any form of employment law violations.
"Operations like these demonstrate the continuous commitment of the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency alongside other enforcement agencies in ensuring that every employer complies with the prevailing laws, thereby curbing any form of human trafficking and labour exploitation," he said.
He said the public can provide any information related to criminal activities at sea or maritime offences to the Perak Maritime Operations Centre at 05-683 8737 or the emergency line 999 for immediate action.

Title: Michigan primary offers key test of Democratic voters' views on Israel
Article:
MICHIGAN voters head to the polls on Tuesday in a high-stakes Democratic Senate primary that could shape the battle for control of Congress and the future of the Democratic Party amid a fierce internal debate over US support for Israel.
The contest pits Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive former public health official who wants to end unconditional US military aid to Israel and accuses it of genocide, against US Representative Haley Stevens, a moderate backed by pro-Israel groups and a longtime outspoken supporter of Israel.
The race is the latest battleground between progressives and moderates over US support for Israel, an issue that has played out in primaries nationwide this year.
But unlike contests in liberal bastions, this is a statewide race in a critical Midwestern swing state ahead of November's midterms — a seat Democrats must win in the fight for Senate control.
The outcome could offer the clearest signal yet of whether Democratic voters are more receptive to an anti-establishment message hostile to Israel and big money in politics, or a more moderate approach supportive of Israel, according to analysts and party strategists interviewed by Reuters.
Frank Lowenstein, a former special envoy for Israeli-Palestinian negotiations under President Barack Obama, said the primary was a bellwether for Democrats' ideological future and could shape how their 2028 presidential candidates approach relations with Israel.
"This will help inform them about how tough to be on Israel," he said. "It's teed up to be a pretty clear choice."
Israel's favourability rating among Democrats fell from 59 per cent in 2018 to 22 per cent in May, according to Reuters/Ipsos polling.
But, the primary is also a test of broader voter frustrations over economic concerns and the party establishment, Democratic strategists said.
An El-Sayed win would underscore the anger fuelling demand for new leadership — and the appeal of his call to reinvest taxpayer dollars at home rather than in Israel's war in Gaza.
A Stevens win would signal she made her case despite anti-establishment headwinds, with economic concerns and the desire to beat Republicans outweighing Israel.
"Either way, Democratic leaders shouldn't ignore the anger at the status quo fueLling El-Sayed's campaign or assume a Stevens win lets the party off the hook," Democratic strategist Karen Finney said.
Voters in Michigan, Virginia and Washington State will also be deciding on US House candidates in Democratic primaries on Tuesday, including a handful that could decide if the party retakes the lower chamber.
Four of those races are considered general election toss-ups.
[[nid:1504122]]
The winner of the Senate primary will face former Republican Representative Mike Rogers, a vocal supporter of Israel in a state President Donald Trump narrowly won in 2024.
El-Sayed has been endorsed by and held rallies with two high-profile progressives: Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont, and Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York.
Analysts say one significant factor in his favor is that Michigan is home to some of the country's largest Arab-American communities, where hostility to Israel runs deep.
Recent polls show El-Sayed leading by an average of eight percentage points, although one Detroit News survey in early July had Stevens up by seven percentage points.
El-Sayed supports progressive causes like universal healthcare, abolishing US Immigration and Customs Enforcement, and getting corporate money out of politics.
He told Reuters in an interview that ending unconditional US military aid to Israel was not just a human rights issue, but about helping American families.
"Gaza and Israel is an affordability issue. I would rather spend our money on healthcare and schools and infrastructure here at home rather than bombing other people elsewhere."
El-Sayed said he had focused on issues affecting Michigan voters, while Democratic leaders had sought to recast the race as a national referendum on the party's future.
Stevens and her allies argue that she would make a stronger general election candidate against Rogers because she is more likely to appeal to independents in a race expected to be decided at the margins.
Stevens has been backed by the party establishment, including Chuck Schumer, the top Senate Democrat, and Gretchen Whitmer, Michigan's two-term governor.
In emailed responses to Reuters, Stevens largely declined to answer questions about Israel or the money she has taken from pro-Israel groups, including over US$30 million from the main super PAC for the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, one of Washington's most influential foreign-policy lobbying organisations.
"No one influences my vote other than the people of Michigan," she said.
Stevens has been critical of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, including in a July debate.
"Mr. Netanyahu has not made us safer, has not brought us closer to peace. And he's endangered Jews here in America and around the world," she said.
* The writer is from Reuters

Title: Providers must verify age via MyKad or passport under new social media rules
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Licensed social media service providers must now implement official document verification, including MyKad or passports, to ensure account holders are aged 16 and above.
In a written reply on the Parliament website today, the Communications Ministry said the mandate is enforced under the Child Protection Code (CPC), which took effect on June 1, 2026.
"Age verification must be carried out using official documents such as MyKad, passports, birth certificates, or other recognised documents. To ensure compliance, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is monitoring the implementation of the CPC by Licensed Service Providers.
"The MCMC has issued written notices under Subsection 30(2) of the Online Safety Act 2025 (Act 866) to social media service providers, requiring them to explain instances of non-compliance and the measures taken to implement age verification mechanisms," the ministry said.
Under Act 866, a convicted provider faces fines of up to RM1 million, plus an additional RM100,000 for each day the offence continues, as well as financial penalties of up to RM10 million.
The ministry was replying to Senator Norhasmimi Abdul Ghani on the effectiveness of Act 866 and the CPC in protecting children from cyberbullying, sexual exploitation, harmful content, and social media addiction.
On online scams, paid advertisements, and fake accounts, the ministry said MCMC submitted 292,102 takedown requests between Jan 1, 2022, and July 31, 2026, with 279,875 items (96 per cent) removed.
For unauthorised advertisements, products, and services, MCMC submitted 20,114 takedown requests, resulting in 17,285 items (86 per cent) being removed.
Over the same period, 17,418 websites were blocked, including 5,103 cases (29 per cent) under MCMC jurisdiction and 12,315 cases (71 per cent) managed by other enforcement agencies.
"Actions such as content removal, account suspension, and website blocking are carried out based on assessments of complaints, platform community guidelines, and applicable laws," the ministry said in response to a question from Senator Musoddak Ahmad regarding platform responsibilities on misleading advertisements.
Addressing 3R (race, religion, and royalty) issues, the ministry said MCMC submitted 14,169 content removal requests between Jan 1, 2022, and June 30, 2026, with 8,750 items (62 per cent) taken down.
MCMC also investigated 462 cases under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (Act 588), prosecuting 22 cases, of which 16 have been concluded and six remain pending.
This was in reply to Senator Mohd Hasbie Muda on enforcement against individuals repeatedly misusing digital platforms to incite provocation or disrupt public order.

Title: 1,404 vessels on watchlist as govt tightens screening of sanctioned ships
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has strengthened its vessel monitoring and screening mechanisms to prevent ships listed under international sanctions from entering Malaysian waters and ports.
In a written reply published on the Parliament website, the Transport Ministry said the measures are being implemented through cooperation among multiple agencies, including the Marine Department, the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA), Customs Department, Immigration Department and police.
According to the ministry, a total of 1,404 vessels have been placed on the MMEA's watchlist and are also listed under various international sanctions regimes, including those of the United States' Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO), the European Union (EU), the United Nations (UN), and the Australian Sanctions Office.
"To prevent vessels on international sanctions lists from entering Malaysian waters through ship renaming, reflagging, or changes in ownership, the government has implemented several control mechanisms.
"These mechanisms include pre-arrival screening of all vessel entry applications and identity verification using the IMO number, which is a unique identification number that remains with a vessel throughout its lifetime," the ministry said.
It was responding to a question from Senator Datuk Wu Him Ven, who asked what legal provisions and mechanisms the government uses to prohibit Israeli vessels, as well as Russian oil tankers, from docking in Malaysia.
The ministry said it also conducts monitoring through the Automatic Identification System (AIS), Vessel Traffic Services (VTS), the Port Management Information System, and other maritime surveillance systems to detect suspicious vessel movements and sailing patterns.
"If there is information indicating that a vessel is linked to activities that violate international sanctions or poses a risk to national security, the government may reject the vessel's application to enter Malaysian waters, deny it permission to dock, or prohibit it from unloading cargo, in accordance with national laws and government policy," the ministry said.
Regarding Israeli vessels, the ministry said that on Dec 20, 2023, the government banned Israeli-registered ships from docking at Malaysian ports; prohibited ships flying the Israeli flag from entering Malaysian ports; and revoked the operating permission of Israeli shipping company ZIM Integrated Shipping Services Ltd.
However, as a maritime nation, Malaysia continues to uphold the principle of innocent passage, in line with its obligations as a State Party to the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), which Malaysia ratified on Oct 14, 1996.
The minisry said the government will continue to strengthen cooperation among domestic agencies and enhance information sharing with international maritime organisations to ensure that Malaysian waters and ports are not exploited by vessels attempting to evade sanctions through flag hopping, ship identity fraud, or changes in ownership structure.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Healthcare, financial services lift Bursa Malaysia higher at the close
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia closed at its intraday high on Tuesday, with gains led by the financial services and healthcare sectors, as investors rotated back into defensive and domestic-oriented sectors amid improving global risk appetite, an analyst said.
At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 6.93 points to 1,732.66 from Monday's close of 1,725.73.
The benchmark index opened 0.21 of a point higher at 1,725.94, and subsequently hit a low of 1,722.78 in early trade before gathering momentum throughout the rest of the day to end at its intraday high.
The broader market was also positive with advancers outpacing decliners 621 to 482, while 581 counters were unchanged, 1,052 untraded and 16 suspended.
Turnover improved to 2.80 billion units valued at RM2.81 billion from 2.73 billion units valued at RM2.33 billion on Monday.
IPP Financial Advisers (IPPFA) director of investment strategy and country economist Mohd Sedek Jantan said market sentiment was supported by the rebound in United States technology stocks, which helped restore confidence in the artificial intelligence (AI) theme.
He said the recovery followed a volatile month marked by concerns over whether heavy AI-related capital expenditure would translate into sustainable earnings growth.
"Despite the improved external backdrop, investors remained selective as geopolitical tensions in West Asia continued to cloud the global outlook, favouring sectors with resilient earnings, stable cash flows and strong domestic fundamentals," he said.
Among the heavyweights, Maybank slid six sen to RM10.78, Public Bank gained eight sen to RM5.28, CIMB Group added two sen to RM8.03, IHH Healthcare climbed 13 sen to RM8.43, and Tenaga Nasional was flat at RM14.50.
As for the most active stocks, Zetrix AI was one sen higher at 73.5 sen, Mr D.I.Y. dropped 10 sen to RM1.52, NationGate Holdings put on six sen to RM1.29, HHRG was unchanged at 11.5 sen, and Dataprep Holdings was one sen lower to six sen.
Leading gainers included Malaysian Pacific Industries, which perked up 70 sen to RM46.72, Kelington Group jumped 52 sen to RM8.72, Kuala Lumpur Kepong and Fraser & Neave garnered 32 sen each to RM21.32 and RM27.82, respectively, and Petronas Dagangan improved 26 sen to RM19.70.
As for top losers, Nestle lost 90 sen to RM101.80, United Plantations and Hong Leong Industries erased 16 sen each to RM34.04 and RM17.84, respectively, while Kim Loong Resources and Gas Malaysia slipped 12 sen each to RM2.66 and RM5.05, respectively.

Title: US has used 'virtually all' of its long-range precision missiles during Iran war
Article:
NEW YORK: The US Army has used up much of its stockpile of highly accurate long-range missiles during its five-month war with Iran, according to three people familiar with the data, raising concerns about the military's readiness for future conflicts.
The missiles are principally the Army's surface-to-surface weapons, known as Army Tactical Missile Systems (ATACMS) and Precision Strike Missiles (PrSM). The US has used "virtually all" of these weapons, according to two of the sources.
The degree to which the military is running out of ATACMS and Precision Strike Missiles has not been previously reported. The long-range munitions are an important part the military's arsenal, allowing accurate strikes from a safe distance.
US-supplied ATACMS have played a key role in the war in Ukraine, allowing Ukrainian forces to attack targets inside Russia. The PrSM is a newer, more advanced generation that will replace the ATACMS, which have a shorter range.
Analysts say such weapons – which cost over US$1 million each – would also be important in any conflict with China.
The sources declined to say how many of each munition the US had left.
President Donald Trump launched the Iran war jointly with Israel in February, predicting that the conflict would last a short time.
But as the war drags on, the three people familiar with the matter expressed worry that the falling missile supplies could limit the US ability to deter adversaries, including Russia and China.
A fourth person familiar with the matter said that while Central Command — which oversees US forces in the Middle East — has nearly used up the land-based missiles it had before the war began, it has been able to reload from US military supplies elsewhere in the world.
The sources interviewed for this story spoke on the condition of anonymity.
Asked for comment on the stockpile data, the White House issued a statement from Trump, saying the US had "far more munitions than anyone in the world" and "far more than we need."
"Our defence companies are, at this moment, making more munitions than they have ever made before, in addition to expanding their plants and equipment at record levels," Trump said.
Analysts agree that certain munitions, including artillery shells and several types of missiles, are being produced at record levels but caution that supplies might far short of what is needed for a prolonged war.
Lockheed Martin, which makes the ATACMs and PrSMs, along with the anti-ballistic missile THAAD system, did not immediately respond to questions about Trump's statements or about supply levels. Raytheon, which makes Tomahawk missiles and Patriot interceptors, two important US weapons, also did not immediately respond.
Responding to a request for comment, chief Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said: "America's military is the most powerful in the world and has everything it needs to execute at the time and place of the President's choosing.
"We have executed multiple successful operations across combatant commands while ensuring the US military possesses a deep arsenal of capabilities to protect our people and our interests."
[[nid:1504106]]
The supply figures have circulated inside the federal government over the last week during tense conversations inside the Trump administration about how much longer the US can continue striking Iran without drawing down the stockpile to levels that would limit the military's ability to respond to crises elsewhere.
One of the sources said the drawdown of the ATACMS and PrSM stockpiles reflected a decision by the Trump administration to avoid riskier ways of attacking Iranian targets, such as by using piloted aircraft to drop bombs.
Because these weapons allow the military to attack targets from a distance, analysts say they would be valuable in a war against an adversary with strong air defences, such as China.
They have been used to strike targets inside Iran, according to a March report by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS).
According to the report, PrSM stockpiles were low to start with, since it is a relatively new munition, but the US military has ordered a large number of them for 2027. The Army has said that ATACMS are being phased out and that production is shifting to the newer PrSM missiles.
Military leaders have for weeks warned the president that stockpiles of defensive weapons — including Patriot interceptors, which are effective against ballistic missiles — were dwindling, said two of the sources.
Last week, several media outlets reported Trump had decided not to launch another massive offensive inside Iran in part because his military advisers had warned about the US stockpile.
A US official disputed those accounts, saying Trump chose not to move forward with another attack because of pressure from Gulf states.
The Middle East conflict has sparked intense debate about Trump's authority to prosecute hostilities against Iran without congressional authorisation.
No request for a declaration of war or an authorisation to use military force has been submitted to Congress.
Last week, CSIS published a report estimating that between February and July about 65 per cent of Patriot interceptors had been expended and that the number of THAAD ballistic missile interceptors in US. stockpiles was at least 38 per cent lower than at the start of the war.
Patriots and THAADs are systems that detect and destroy incoming missiles and are among the most effective in the country's arsenal.
While Reuters has not seen the supply figures, those numbers match internal US data, two of the sources said.
The US also burned through a little less than half of its global supply of Tomahawk cruise missiles, which are generally launched from ships, since the start of the war, one of the sources said.
Reuters could not independently verify that number.
The Tomahawk is a Navy weapon, launched from destroyers, cruisers and submarines, and has long served as the sea service's principal means of striking heavily defended targets without risking pilots.
Raytheon, a unit of RTX, has reached a tentative multi-year agreement with the Pentagon aimed at boosting Tomahawk production, alongside increases in other munitions, as Washington races to rebuild stockpiles.

Title: Security expert: Malaysian pilot arrested in Jakarta jeopardised lives by flying 'high'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The arrest of a Malaysia Airlines pilot in Indonesia for alleged drug smuggling is a wake-up call for the entire aviation industry, not just the national carrier.
National Defence University of Malaysia (UPNM) Professor Dr Mohd Mizan Mohammad Aslam said the case was particularly alarming because the pilot was not merely smuggling drugs — he had also been under the influence of narcotics while operating a passenger flight.
"It jeopardises the life of the people he was piloting," he told the
New Straits Times
.
Previously, it was reported that the
pilot was arrested
for allegedly attempting to smuggle a large quantity of drugs, including more than 70,000 ecstasy pills weighing 25kg into Indonesia last week.
A urine test showed that the 39-year-old tested positive for methamphetamine, MDMA and cocaine.
Mizan called for two key long-term reforms.
The first was digitalisation — replacing manual checkpoints with automated detection systems to remove the human element, which he said was prone to tolerance and corruption.
"When we do things manually, people tend to tolerate and be corrupted. Let a digital system do everything.
"Once there is a problem highlighted by the system, then the person has to be investigated," he said.
He said the pilot had made no effort to conceal the drugs, suggesting he believed his status as a crew member conferred immunity from scrutiny.
"The way this pilot carried this contraband — it was not something he tried to hide. He just put it in his bag like he was carrying food.
"He thought he had immunity because he is an airline crew member, so he could just pass through the checkpoints without any issues," he said.
The second reform Mizan called for was the institutionalisation of scheduled security drills and checks, conducted consistently and not merely in response to incidents.
He warned against the recurring tendency to mobilise vigorously in the immediate aftermath of a crisis, only to revert to complacency once public attention had faded.
Mizan said the incident should prompt all airlines and airports — not only Malaysia Airlines and KLIA — to review their screening procedures for crew members and staff, adding that he welcomed the swift response by the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) and the Transport Ministry to the matter.
Yesterday, the Transport Ministry convened a special meeting with aviation, border security and law enforcement agencies to
review airport security
procedures following the arrest of the pilot.
The meeting, chaired by ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Jana Santhiran Muniayan, brought together representatives from the police, MCBA, Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG), Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) and other agencies.
Indonesian authorities found 2.74g of methamphetamine, as well as 0.0825g of methamphetamine residue in a glass pipe, when the pilot was arrested at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta Airport.

Title: CAAM seeks public, industry feedback on Low Altitude Economy framework
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) has invited industry players, government agencies, academia and members of the public to submit feedback by Sept 2 on a proposed national framework that will chart the country's Low Altitude Economy (LAE).
CAAM chief executive officer Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud said the proposed Malaysia LAE Framework is aimed at providing the country's long-term strategic direction for developing a safe, secure, sustainable and commercially viable low-altitude aviation ecosystem.
He said the framework aims to unlock the potential of emerging technologies, including Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS), Advanced Air Mobility (AAM), artificial intelligence (AI), autonomous systems and digital connectivity, to transform service delivery across sectors such as logistics, agriculture, infrastructure inspection, emergency response and environmental monitoring, while paving the way for future passenger mobility.
Norazman said the public consultation represents an important step in translating Malaysia's LAE ambitions into a coordinated and implementable national framework
"Malaysia has the industrial capabilities, talent and technological foundations to build a competitive LAE. However, its success will depend on having a clear direction and close coordination among regulators, government agencies, industry, academia, technology developers, investors and the wider public," he said in a statement here today.
He said the consultation gives stakeholders the opportunity to help shape a framework that supports innovation and commercial growth while ensuring aviation safety, security and public confidence remain at the centre of its development.
He said the proposed framework was developed following feedback gathered during the Malaysia Low Altitude Economy Forum 2026 held on June 24 and is intended to complement the 13th Malaysia Plan, the New Industrial Master Plan 2030, the Malaysian Aerospace Industry Blueprint 2030 and the Malaysia Drone Technology Action Plan 2022-2030.
"The framework will set out the definition and scope of the LAE, its Vision, Mission and Guiding Principles, as well as four Strategic Pillars: Safe Aircraft, Safe Operations, Connected Infrastructure and Thriving Industry. These are supported by key enabling foundations and a phased Implementation Roadmap for the development of Malaysia's LAE ecosystem."
Norazman said CAAM is inviting written feedback from industry players, government agencies, academia, professional bodies, investors and members of the public before finalising the framework.
The Public Consultation Paper is available on CAAM's website via the link: Proposed Malaysia_ Low_ Altitude Economy Framework and all written submissions must be emailed to lae.policy@caam.gov.my by Sept 2.

Title: HLB bags six regional, international awards in wealth management
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Leong Bank Bhd (HLB) has clinched six regional and international wealth management awards, with its HLB Private Bank and HLB Priority businesses recognised for their offerings to high-net-worth and emerging affluent clients.
The awards come as the bank accelerates the expansion of its wealth management business under its three to five-year transformation plan.
The plan focuses on innovation and personalised wealth management solutions.
HLB Private Bank was named Best Private Bank/Wealth Manager in Malaysia and Singapore at the WealthBriefingAsia Awards, while HLB Priority won Best Bank/Wealth Manager for Emerging Affluent Clients at the Global Mass Affluent Banking Awards.
HLB Private also received the Rising Star Private Bank Award for Malaysia and Best Private Bank for Wealth Creation & Preservation at the Global Private Banking Innovation Awards.
HLB Priority was further recognised with the Best Value Proposition for Emerging Affluent Clients award at the Global Mass Affluent Banking Awards.
The bank said the accolades reflect the progress it has made in expanding wealth management as a key pillar of its long-term growth strategy, despite being a relatively new entrant in the region's private wealth landscape.
Group managing director and chief executive officer Kevin Lam said strengthening the bank's wealth management capabilities is central to its transformation agenda.
This enables it to diversify its income base while supporting customers throughout their wealth creation journey.
"We are in the business of growing wealth and elevating our wealth management capabilities is a core priority of our ongoing bankwide transformation plan.
"While this naturally helps us diversify our revenue through non-interest income, its true value lies in how we support clients as they succeed and grow their wealth," he said in a statement.
As part of the strategy, the bank recently hosted its inaugural Private Markets Summit in Malaysia.
It announced plans to launch two investment products - the Global Private Equity Fund-of-Funds II and the Private Markets Evergreen Income Fund (Resilient Income Generation).
The funds are designed to provide eligible investors with access to private market opportunities that have traditionally been available mainly to institutional investors.
HLB managing director and regional head of wealth management Jeffrey Yap said rising market volatility, geopolitical uncertainty and increasing demand for intergenerational wealth planning are reshaping clients' investment needs.
"The ultimate differentiator for us now lies in our ability to provide clients access to the best the global landscape has to offer, whether that means global market insights, sophisticated regional investment options, or market-leading advisory services," he said.
HLB has partnered with Lombard Odier to provide portfolio advisory and succession planning services for high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients.
The bank also introduced artificial intelligence-powered tools for its relationship managers to support investment advisory.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 149 state food production zones gazetted
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 149 out of 176 permanent food production zones under state government jurisdiction have been gazetted to date, said Deputy Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Chan Foong Hin.
He said the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry, through the Agriculture Department, the Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) and the Fisheries Department (DOF), stands ready to collaborate with state governments to identify, develop and gazette potential areas, including suburban areas.
"All Permanent Food Production Parks (TKPM), Permanent Ruminant Production Parks (TKPR) and Aquaculture Industrial Zone (ZIA) projects are regulated by the three departments.
"The performance of land tenants is also assessed regularly, while technical guidance is provided to ensure that no operator is left behind," he said.
He was replying to a question from Senator Datuk Koh Nai Kwong on the federal government's measures to ensure farmers and smallholders are not sidelined in the implementation of the initiative.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Stratus surges to record high on growing interest in semicon automation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Stratus Global Holdings Bhd closed at a record high today, extending since its Main Market debut last month amid growing investor interest in the semiconductor automation specialist.
The stock closed 21 sen, or 10 per cent, higher at RM2.31, with more than 14.7 million shares traded.
The gain valued the company at RM2.59 billion, making it the seventh-biggest gainer on Bursa Malaysia.
The share price opened at RM2.10 and climbed as much as 26 sen, or 12.4 per cent, to an intraday high of RM2.36.
At the midday break, the counter settled at RM2.29, up 19 sen, or 9.05 per cent, with 9.7 million shares changing hands.
Stratus Global has been among the market's strongest-performing initial public offerings this year.
The Main Market-listed company made a stellar debut on July 21, with its shares closing at RM2.11, up 183 per cent from its initial public offering (IPO) price of 80 sen.
On the same day, the Employees Provident Fund emerged as the company's fourth-largest shareholder after acquiring a 5.08 per cent stake, or 63.5 million shares.
The fund subsequently trimmed its holding marginally to 5.06 per cent, or 63.25 million shares, on July 22.
The Penang-based firm specialises in factory automation solutions, particularly cleanroom automated material handling system (AMHS) solutions for the semiconductor industry.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd has initiated coverage on Stratus Global with a "buy" call and a fair value of RM1.56, based on 28 times its projected  financial year 2027 (FY27) earnings per share.
Its analyst Crystal Chin said Stratus Global is well positioned to benefit from rising capital expenditure in the semiconductor industry, driven by artificial intelligence (AI), supported by its strong profitability, debt-free balance sheet and fully funded expansion plans.
The firm forecasts Stratus Global to post core net profit of RM69.7 million in FY27 and RM84.8 million in FY28.
She noted that although FY26 revenue eased to RM197.1 million as several legacy projects were completed, the company secured more than RM112 million in hybrid AMHS revenue from new customers, providing a platform for future upgrades and expansion work.
Chin expects these new customer wins to contribute more meaningfully from FY27 onwards, as AMHS forms part of the core infrastructure of semiconductor manufacturing facilities.
To strengthen its global presence, Stratus Global has allocated RM20 million over the next three years to establish sales and engineering support offices in Japan, Taiwan, Germany and the United States.
North America and Europe accounted for more than 81.7 per cent of FY26 revenue.
"Engineering support on the ground is vital as it shortens response times on installation and commissioning, which matters when systems are custom-built to each fab's layout.
"It also positions Stratus closer to the four markets where new fab construction is concentrated.
"The strength of underlying demand is reflected in the number of completed AMHS projects, which rose from 26 in FY23 to 45 in FY26," she said in a note.
The company is also expanding its manufacturing capacity by investing RM122.6 million, or 43 per cent of its IPO proceeds, in a new multi-storey production facility opposite its existing plant in Bayan Lepas.
The new facility, expected to begin operations in phases from the third quarter of 2028, will increase built-up space to at least 170,000 sq ft, including 100,000 sq ft of production area, roughly doubling its current manufacturing footprint.
Chin said Stratus Global's competitive advantage lies in its ability to develop both its AMHS hardware and proprietary IntelliMove control software in-house, enabling it to achieve significantly higher profitability than larger global peers.
Stratus Global currently has an order book of RM108.4 million across 49 contracts, with RM75.4 million scheduled for recognition in FY27.
It also held RM121.7 million in cash at the end of FY26 and remains debt-free, while management has committed to a dividend payout of at least 25 per cent of annual net profit.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 46 accidents, 11 deaths during RXZ Members 8.0 programme
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 46 road accident cases involving motorcyclists were recorded in a four-day period starting from July 30 to last Sunday, during the RXZ Members 8.0 programme.
Bukit Aman Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) director Datuk Seri Muhammed Hasbullah Ali said that of the total, 11 cases or 23.91 per cent were fatal accidents, five cases (10.87 per cent) were serious accidents and 30 cases (65.22 per cent) were minor accidents.
According to the daily breakdown, four cases were recorded on July 30, 16 cases on July 31, 11 cases on Aug 1 and 15 cases Aug 2 involving a total of 44 male and two female victims, he said.
"Analysis of the age profile found that the group aged between 21 and 30 recorded the highest involvement, namely 19 people, followed by the age group of 18 to 20 years (10), 41 to 50 years (nine) and 31 to 40 years (eight)," he said in a statement via the official TEID Facebook page today.
Hasbullah said the analysis also found that the type of rear-end collision accident recorded the highest number with 21 cases, followed by skidding (15), side collision (seven) and vehicle grazing (three).
He said all 11 fatal accident cases were being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, while five serious accident cases were being investigated under Section 43(1) of the same act and minor accident cases were being investigated under the provisions of the relevant Traffic Rules.
"Among the factors identified as contributing to accidents are negligence, failure to control the vehicle, following too closely and unsafe riding that can endanger oneself and other road users," he said.
Hasbullah advised motorcyclists to always obey the speed limit, maintain a safe distance, avoid uncontrolled group movement, do not race or perform dangerous actions and ensure that the motorcycle is in a safe condition before starting the journey.
He also recommended that organisers of motorcycle programmes or gatherings prepare an orderly movement plan, provide safety briefings to participants and cooperate with the authorities to reduce the risk of accidents.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Suhakam expresses deep concern after appeals court upholds stay on Pastor Koh probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) has expressed deep concern over the Court of Appeal's decision to uphold a stay of the High Court's orders in the enforced disappearance case of Pastor Raymond Koh.
It said the decision may further impede efforts to establish the truth and ensure accountability in a case that has remained unresolved for more than nine years.
"The passage of time inevitably increases the risk that evidence may deteriorate, witnesses may become unavailable and investigative opportunities be irretrievably lost," the commission said in a statement.
The
High Court ruled on Nov 5, 2025,
in favour of Pastor Koh's family, finding the Malaysian government and police liable for his abduction and enforced disappearance in 2017.
However, on Jan 26, the Court of Appeal stayed the High Court order requiring police to recommence investigations into his disappearance.
On
July 29, the Court of Appeal also dismissed
an application by Koh's wife, Susanna Liew, to lift the stay.
Suhakam said in its landmark 2019 Public Inquiry it had concluded that Pastor Koh was the victim of an enforced disappearance carried out by agents of the state — a finding the High Court similarly upheld when it ordered investigations to be reopened.
"Those findings represented an important step towards accountability and offered renewed hope to the family that the truth would finally be uncovered," Suhakam said.
The commission highlighted that delays in enforced disappearance cases prolonged the suffering of families involved and is a denial of justice.
Suhakam reiterated that investigations into alleged enforced disappearances must be prompt, thorough, independent, impartial and effective.
They added that accountability was indispensable to uphold public confidence in the rule of law.
The commission renewed its call for Malaysia to ratify the International Convention for the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance and to criminalise enforced disappearance as a distinct offence under domestic law.
"Suhakam stands in solidarity with the family of Pastor Raymond Koh in their continued pursuit of truth and justice," it said.
On Friday, Liew appealed directly to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to intervene after the Court of Appeal's decision.
In their Nov 5 ruling, High Court Judge Datuk Su Tiang Joo ordered police to recommence investigation of the case and report to the Attorney-General's Chambers about its progress every two months.
He also ordered the removal of the initial investigators from the case.
Koh was abducted by a group of armed men while driving along Jalan SS4B/10 in Petaling Jaya.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lula, Brazil's political titan, races against time
Article:
SHIRTLESS and drenched in sweat on his treadmill, Lula runs. He keeps running.
At 80, President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, the dominant figure in Brazilian politics for four decades, wants to show he still has the energy to win a fourth term in office in October's election.
"You can't stop the Earth from turning or the years from passing," Lula muses in his gravelly voice in one of the social media videos he shares showcasing his workouts.
The leftist leader has survived electoral defeats, 580 days in prison, and the disgrace of a corruption conviction which, although later annulled, still prompts taunts from the right of "Lula the thief."
He has also survived health scares, notably a fall in his bathroom in 2024 that caused a brain bleed.
Since then, he often wears a Panama hat. His once thick black hair has greyed and thinned, much like his trademark beard.
But he insists he feels fitter than ever and he dreams of "living to 120."
Lula grew up in deep poverty, the seventh of eight children born to a family of illiterate farmers in the arid northeastern state of Pernambuco.
He worked as a shoeshine boy and peanut vendor before becoming a metalworker and trade unionist. In the 1960s, he lost a finger in a workplace accident.
After losing three presidential bids, Lula finally entered the presidential palace in Brasilia in 2003 and was re-elected in 2006.
He left office in 2010 as a blue-collar hero who presided over a commodity-fuelled economic boom that helped lift 30 million people out of poverty.
But massive corruption scandals haunted Lula and his party, fuelling a wave of disgust that propelled far-right leader Jair Bolsonaro into the presidency in 2018.
Lula was jailed later that year until the charges were thrown out on procedural grounds and the lead judge on the case was found to be biased.
However, Lula was not exonerated and the scandal contributed to an enduring polarisation in Brazil.
Bolsonaro's presidency was equally divisive, and by the 2022 election, Lula pulled off a dramatic comeback by a razor-thin margin.
[[nid:1504084]]
Bolsonaro was later sentenced to 27 years in prison for attempting a coup after trying to prevent Lula from returning to power.
Back in office, Lula at first seemed out of step with a Brazil he appeared to be rediscovering.
He lives without a cellphone in a hyper-connected nation of 213 million people that is flooded with disinformation.
Lula is credited with restoring social programmes dismantled by his predecessor, curbing the destruction of the Amazon rainforest, and putting Brazil's democracy back on a more secure footing.
His third term, however, has had the feel of a pale remake, with few genuinely new ideas. The father of five still provokes fierce rejection among voters frustrated by inflation, crime and corruption.
In 2022, Lula said he would not seek another term in office.
So why take on presidential hopeful Flavio Bolsonaro, the 45-year-old senator and eldest son of his greatest political rival?
Lula, who has not cultivated a potential successor, says he wants to stop the far right from returning to "destroy" the country.
"He's in great shape," an anonymous foreign diplomat told AFP, describing Lula as a "campaign beast."
Flavio Bolsonaro is less complimentary: "The Brazilian Biden is grumpy, irresponsible, and has become a danger to our nation. When you look at Lula, you don't see a future."
Joe Biden is, for Lula, the ultimate cautionary tale. The then-octogenarian US president's public decline during the 2024 election campaign clearly left an impression on the Brazilian leader.
His tireless travel schedule and quick wit testify to his stamina – and he also credits his third wife Rosangela da Silva, 59, with keeping him young.
If he loses in October, Lula would leave office without the triumphant finale he seeks, but with an enduring legacy.
As he reminded foreign media, including AFP, in a 2024 interview: "There is no one in this country with more experience as president than me."
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan DAP to focus solely on unity government motion
Article:
SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan DAP will focus solely on the central leadership's motion on whether the party should remain in the unity government until the end of the parliamentary term at its national congress on Aug 16.
State DAP secretary Cha Kee Chin said the chapter would not submit any additional motions at the annual congress.
"We are not bringing any other motion. Our focus is strictly on the single motion from the central leadership to decide whether DAP will remain in the unity government or otherwise," he said when contacted today.
He said delegates would debate and decide on the motion at the congress, adding that there had been a misunderstanding that state chapters would submit their own motions.
"This is an annual congress, not an extraordinary general meeting. Our focus remains strictly on DAP's position in the unity government," said Cha, who is also Rasah MP.
DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke had yesterday clarified that the motion would be tabled at the congress following a decision by the party's Central Executive Committee (CEC).
Cha urged delegates to attend, deliberate on the motion and make a decision in the best interest of the party's future direction.
He acknowledged that the motion had drawn public attention following DAP's disappointing performance in the Negri Sembilan state election last Saturday.
Loke lost the Chennah seat, which he had held for three terms, to Barisan Nasional candidate Siow Kong Choon, while DAP also lost the Repah seat contested by S. Veerapan.
However, DAP and Pakatan Harapan retained several seats, including Seremban Jaya, Mambau, Rahang, Lukut, Bukit Kepayang, Nilai, Bahau and Temiang.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: IRB raises RM4.4b in additional tax assessments as of June 30
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Inland Revenue Board (IRB) has raised RM4.4 billion in additional tax assessments as of June 30, said its chief executive officer Datuk Dr Abu Tariq Jamaluddin.
He said this reflects IRB's commitment to protecting the country's revenue and strengthening the integrity of the taxation system.
"The IRB focuses on implementing strategic risk-based audit and compliance activities to detect and address significant cases of non-compliance, including tax evasion and aggressive tax planning.
"This approach is important to ensure that the fairness of the tax system is maintained and every taxpayer fulfils his responsibilities fairly," he said at the 26th National Taxation Conference's opening ceremony here today.
He said the use of artificial intelligence (AI) has empowered the IRB's decision-making process and strengthened risk management through more sophisticated data analysis.
"AI has empowered the IRB's data analytics capabilities by enabling the processing, scrutiny and analysis of more than 1.6 billion e-Invoices received to date.
"This capability allows transaction patterns to be identified quickly and accurately, thus increasing the effectiveness of compliance risk detection, strengthening the integrity of tax data and supporting a more data-based decision-making process," he said.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan launched the event.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lebanon's negotiations with Israel bring 'shame and humiliation': Hizbollah
Article:
BEIRUT: Hizbollah leader Naim Qassem said on Tuesday that direct negotiations between Lebanon and Israel would bring "nothing but shame, humiliation, and successive compromises" for Lebanon, ahead of new talks in Rome.
In a televised address, Qassem said Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun "has not acted as an arbiter, nor as a unifying figure, but has become biased and divisive, which is incompatible with his role and with Lebanon's strength."
In another matter, Qassem said Tuesday that he had no objection to meeting with Syria's leadership, the first time he has expressed such a stance, after his Iran-backed group fought for Syria's former authorities that were ousted in 2024.
"There is no impediment to a public meeting between Hizbollah and the Syrian leadership at a time considered appropriate by both sides," Qassem said in a televised address, emphasising "the importance and necessity of positive, fraternal, cooperative relations".
Hizbollah for years fought in support of longtime Syrian ruler Bashar al-Assad in the country's civil war, and Syria served as a key supply route to Lebanon from Iran before the new authorities seized power in December 2024.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 5-year-old survivor of Bentong tree crash in stable condition
Article:
KUANTAN: The 5-year-old sole survivor of yesterday's tree crash tragedy in Bentong, which claimed the lives of four family members, is in stable condition at Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital (Hoshas), Temerloh.
Pahang Health director Dr Saiful Azlan Sharif said Muhammad Rizz Haziq Mohd Radzi, who suffered minor injuries to his face and head, was receiving treatment at the hospital and remained in stable condition.
"The victim's recovery is being closely monitored, and he is receiving appropriate care and support," he said when contacted today.
Rizz Haziq was travelling
with his family when the Ford Ranger Raptor they were in was crushed by a fallen tree along the old Kuala Lumpur-Bentong Road near Janda Baik.
The incident
claimed the lives
of his father, Maran Umno Youth chief Mohd Radzi Rahimi; mother Nuraini Mohammad Jafri, 36; twin brother Muhammad Rizz Hazim; and uncle Mohammad Nizam Mohammad Jafri, 35.
Meanwhile, Radzi's father, Rahimi Abd Samad, 63, said the family had yet to decide who would care for Rizz Haziq.
"Perhaps his mother's family in Jerantut will take care of him, but nothing has been discussed yet," he said.
An image of Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail
carrying Rizz Haziq at Kampung Paya Luas Mosque in Temerloh, where the victims' remains were bathed and shrouded yesterday, went viral on social media.
The four victims were buried in a single grave at the Sri Chedung Muslim Cemetery in Maran.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Termite infestation blamed for heritage shophouse collapse in Penang
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A termite-damaged wooden beam caused the collapse at a heritage shophouse in Lebuh Armenian, injuring two Sri Lankan tourists today.
State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman Jason H'ng said inspections found the building's wooden beam had deteriorated after being infested by termites before it gave way.
Following the incident, he said the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) had been asked to take the initiative to carry out pest control measures in the area, although maintenance of privately owned buildings remained the responsibility of their owners.
"The area is a heritage site, but the buildings are still privately owned. Therefore, owners must be responsible for maintaining their respective buildings.
"Although it is the responsibility of building owners, I have asked the local authority to take the initiative to carry out termite control because this heritage area is a major tourist attraction," he said when contacted today.
He urged all building owners to engage engineers or building surveyors to conduct regular inspections to ensure their structures remain safe.
Earlier, it was reported that
two Sri Lankan
tourists were injured after being struck by falling masonry and timber from a first-floor beam of a
heritage building
in Lebuh Armenian.
In the
1.11pm incident
, a 66-year-old man and a 55-year-old woman sustained injuries and were taken to hospital for further treatment.
The tourists were understood to be scheduled to return to Sri Lanka tomorrow.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 4 teachers testify in Bandar Utama school murder trial
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Four teachers took the witness stand today in the murder trial of a 15-year-old boy, giving evidence about the events that unfolded inside SMK Bandar Utama Damansara (4) on the day of the fatal stabbing incident last year.
The boy's lawyer, Kitson Foong, who briefed the media on the closed-door proceedings, said the teachers' testimony focused on what happened in and around the school toilet before continuing with events in the school compound.
The teachers were Nursyazwani Saari, Syaza Sahira Abdul Jalil, Muhammad Alif Abdul Razak and Mohd Qauyyum Firdaus Juhar.
"They testified up to the point of how they intervened to stop the boy, regain control of the situation and recover the knife.
"One of the teachers also testified about helping to place the girl (the 16-year-old deceased) onto a stretcher.
"So those are the parts of the story that happened inside the school from the teachers' point of view," said Foong.
Foong said only a few points required clarification during cross-examination.
Following their testimony, Foong commended the teachers for their courage and decisive actions during the incident, saying they deserved recognition for helping restore order in a frightening situation.
"Everybody was obviously scared. These teachers need to be praised for their bravery, raising the standard for teachers.
"Give them some glory. They need to be praised for their bravery and their assistance," he said.
The teenager, who cannot be publicly identified or photographed as he is a minor, was brought to the courtroom from the Puncak Alam Correction Centre, a juvenile detention facility.
The proceedings are being held in camera.
According to the charge sheet, the boy is accused of murdering his schoolmate in the girls' toilet of SMK Bandar Utama Damansara (4), Bandar Utama, Petaling Jaya, between 9.20am and 9.35am on Oct 14 last year.
The victim was a Form Four student.
The charge carries the death penalty, or imprisonment of not less than 30 years and not more than 40 years, and 12 strokes of the rotan upon conviction.
However, under Section 97(1) of the Child Act 2001, the death sentence cannot be imposed on a child at the time of the offence.
Instead, Section 97(2) stipulates that a person convicted of such an offence shall be detained at the pleasure of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong if the offence occurred in the Federal Territories, or the Ruler or Yang di-Pertua Negeri if it occurred in a state.
Foong said two child witnesses are scheduled to testify when the trial resumes tomorrow before High Court judge Adlin Abdul Majid.
Deputy public prosecutors Aqharie Durranie Aziz and Ahmad Iqbal Azman appeared for the prosecution.
Also with Foong were Chew Jee San, Angel Choo and Yan Zhi Wei.
Lawyer Jason Lim Jie Sheng held a watching brief on behalf of the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: More remains found at second Kosovo mass grave
Article:
PRISTINA: Kosovo authorities confirmed late Monday that the remains of four people were found at a second mass grave in the country's north, as investigations into a suspected 1990s war crime continue.
The discovery comes days after the remains of seven people were uncovered at a nearby dig site in the area of Zubin Potok – with officials believing there could be as many as 23 people buried near surrounding villages.
"During excavations conducted in Jabuka, the mortal remains of four people were found and exhumed, who, according to initial assessments, belong to victims of enforced disappearance during the war," the Government Commission on Missing Persons announced in a press release.
The remains have now been sent for DNA testing to try to identify them.
But with the remains of 11 people now recovered from the two sites, prosecutors said the excavation and identification could take months.
Police have also arrested three men from the local area in recent days on suspicion of war crimes, according to prosecutors.
The discovered remains most likely belong to "23 Albanians who have been violently abducted, executed" in the spring of 1999, acting Prime Minister Albain Kurti said on Saturday.
The 1998-1999 war between independence-seeking ethnic Albanian fighters and Serbian armed forces killed around 13,000 people and left 4,000 missing.
Decades of work to uncover mass graves have found the remains of thousands, but 1,600 are still missing.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bukit Aman to probe second Malaysian drug arrest in Indonesia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bukit Aman has begun looking into the arrest of another Malaysian in Indonesia over alleged drug trafficking, just a few days after a Malaysia Airlines pilot was detained in Jakarta on similar allegations.
Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan confirmed that police would follow up on the latest case involving a 22-year-old Malaysian from Johor who was arrested at Juanda International Airport in Surabaya.
"Yes. Bukit Aman NCID will also follow up on this case," Hussein told the
New Straits Times
.
He added that the suspect was arrested with four packets containing a kilogramme of methamphetamine and 1,000 ecstasy pills.
"The packets were wrapped around the suspects body," he said.
The 22-year-old suspect was
detained at Terminal 2
of the Juanda International Airport after arriving on Batik Air flight OD352 from Kuala Lumpur on Monday.
According to Indonesian news portal Jakarta Globe, authorities discovered four packages containing 990g of methamphetamine and another four packages containing 1,089 ecstasy pills strapped beneath a corset worn around the suspect's body.
Investigators said the suspect allegedly admitted to agreeing to act as a drug courier for an international syndicate due to financial difficulties and mounting debts.
"The suspect tried to conceal the narcotics under the corset he was wearing to avoid inspection. However, the attempt was foiled," Juanda naval air base commander Colonel Henoch Nasairus Virzawan was quoted as telling reporters.
Authorities estimated the seized drugs were worth about US$155,000 on the street, adding that the seizure could have prevented the narcotics from reaching an estimated 6,584 users.
Bukit Aman is already
working closely
with its Indonesian counterparts on the pilot's case, with investigations focusing on the source of the drugs, possible syndicate links and how the narcotics managed to leave Malaysia undetected.
The latest arrest comes a week after a Malaysia Airlines pilot was detained at Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport for allegedly attempting to smuggle more than 70,000 ecstasy pills into Indonesia.
Malaysian police are working closely with their Indonesian counterparts in the pilot's case, including tracing the source of the drugs, determining whether he was linked to a syndicate and investigating how the narcotics were able to pass through airport security in Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah, Petronas launch digital platforms to strengthen oil and gas workforce
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah state government has partnered with Petronas to strengthen the state's oil and gas workforce through the development of two online platforms aimed at improving access to employment, training and work pass services.
The national oil company funded the Permohonan Online Pekerjaan dan Latihan Dalam Industri Minyak dan Gas (Pomigas) and the Sabah Work Pass Online System, both managed by the Chief Minister's Department's Home Affairs and Research Office.
Pomigas is a centralised online platform integrated with the Sabah Jobs Portal ecosystem, providing job matching and training opportunities while connecting local talent with industry needs.
The Sabah Work Pass Online System streamlines the submission and management of work pass applications in Sabah by allowing employers to submit documents, track application status and facilitate processing with immigration and labour authorities.
Pomigas began operations earlier this year, while the Sabah Work Pass Online System will be operational from Sept 1.
The two systems were launched by Chief Minister's Department State, Home Affairs and Research secretary Datuk Awang Shahminan Awang Sahari during the Sabah Oil & Gas Industry Talent Alignment Forum (SOGITAF) 2.0 today.
Also present was Petronas Human Resource for Upstream and Malaysia Petroleum Management senior general manager Maria Teo.
Awang Shahminan said the platforms reflected the collaborative efforts between the Sabah government and Petronas to strengthen the state's oil and gas workforce ecosystem.
Petronas Sabah and Labuan Regional Office general manager Datuk Siti Ayu Abdul Wahab said the company remained committed to developing Sabah's local talent through initiatives that enhance workforce capabilities and improve access to industry opportunities.
"Petronas remains focused on unlocking the potential of Sabah's local talent by supporting initiatives that enhance workforce capabilities, improve access to industry opportunities, and contribute towards building a skilled and future-ready oil and gas workforce," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ukraine will never join Nato, former top commander says
Article:
KYIV: Ukraine's ex-army chief Valery Zaluzhny has said the country, fighting a Russian invasion since 2022, will "never" join Nato despite Kyiv's stated intention to become a member of the US-led military alliance.
Zaluzhny, an ultra-popular former top commander whom Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy sacked in 2024, delivered the comments at a meeting of Kyiv's ambassadors on Monday, according to the European Pravda news outlet.
"I know Nato very well. For roughly 12 years I've personally worked on mastering Nato standards, and every year I've listened to the same fairytale that we're about to join," Zaluzhny was quoted as saying.
"Unfortunately, we never will," added Zaluzhny, currently the Ukrainian ambassador to Britain.
He said that "given the current level of development of the Ukrainian Armed Forces" it was impossible for Ukraine to join the alliance that, according to Zaluzhny, "adheres to doctrines dating from the Second World War."
Ukraine prides itself on its military industry progress, particularly in drone technology, which it has extensively developed since Russia invaded four and a half years ago.
In an opinion piece for British newspaper The Daily Telegraph published last month, Zaluzhny said the Ukraine war had "exposed uncomfortable questions about whether Nato is equipped for the conflicts of the 21st century."
"Ukraine has every reason to appreciate the support Nato members have provided, and continues to provide.
"But respect for the alliance should not prevent an honest assessment of its shortcomings," he wrote.
He added that "Ukraine's ability to sustain the war depends heavily upon continued backing from its allies."
Zaluzhny remains Ukraine's most trusted public figure, with 73 per cent support, according to a June poll by the Kyiv International Institute of Sociology.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang launches campaign to boost domestic tourism
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang has launched its "Fall in Love with Penang" campaign to encourage Malaysians to rediscover the state and sustain visitor arrivals through the year-end.
State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the campaign marked a shift in strategy to strengthen the domestic market while continuing efforts to attract international visitors.
"Previously, we focused heavily on international markets through roadshows in China, Southeast Asia, India and several other countries.
"This is the first time we are officially launching the campaign for the local market because we want Malaysians to rediscover Penang and our latest tourism products," he said today.
Wong said the state decided to intensify domestic promotions following the prolonged geopolitical crisis in West Asia, which had affected global travel patterns.
He said while Penang had continued promoting itself overseas, the state was now balancing its strategy by placing greater emphasis on domestic tourism.
"We have refreshed our tourism website with new features, introduced new attractions and are taking this opportunity to strengthen our domestic campaign.
"We want to maintain tourism momentum throughout the year with various strategies," he added.
Among the state's latest attractions are the newly reopened Fort Cornwallis and Penang State Museum, which Wong said had received encouraging public response.
He added that recent events, including the George Town Heritage Celebration and George Town Festival, had also contributed positively to the state's tourism performance.
Looking ahead, Wong said Penang was targeting visitors during the Merdeka and school holiday period in August and September, followed by China's Golden Week holiday from Oct 1 to Oct 8.
To support that effort, he said he would lead a delegation comprising Penang Global Tourism and industry players to Guangzhou and Zhuhai next week to engage tourism stakeholders in China's Greater Bay Area ahead of Golden Week.
"We want to strengthen our engagement with industry players there so that when Golden Week arrives, they will consider Penang as a destination," he said.
On the impact of the West Asia conflict, Wong said the state had observed a slowdown in international travel due to higher airfares driven by rising aviation fuel costs.
"Some airlines have reduced flight frequencies to maximise passenger loads. This is not unique to Malaysia; it is happening worldwide. That is why we need to strengthen both our international and domestic promotion efforts," he said.
Wong said the extension of Visit Malaysia Year until 2027 also provided an opportunity for Penang to recalibrate its tourism strategy while sustaining visitor arrivals from both domestic and overseas markets.

Title: Modernise tax system to stay competitive: Amir Hamzah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must modernise its tax system to keep pace with an increasingly digital and interconnected global economy, ensuring the country remains competitive, attracts investment and strengthens its fiscal resilience.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said shifting business models, expanding cross-border transactions and evolving international tax rules required the government to continually refine its tax policy and administration.
He said these efforts had yielded results, with the implementation of e-Invoicing helping the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) collect an extra RM1.01 billion in taxes, while more than 52,000 taxpayers came forward to voluntarily declare their income.
"In an economy that is becoming increasingly digital, interconnected and complex, tax systems around the world must also evolve in tandem with these developments.
"New business models, cross-border transactions and developments in international taxation require governments to continuously modernise their approach to tax policy and administration," he said when officiating the 26th National Tax Conference here today.
Also present were Treasury secretary-general and IRB chairman Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican, IRB chief executive officer Datuk Dr Abu Tariq Jamaluddin, and Chartered Tax Institute of Malaysia president Alan Chung.
Amir Hamzah said e-Invoicing was among the most significant reforms in the country's tax administration landscape as it not only enhanced transparency but also strengthened data integrity and supported a more efficient, technology-driven compliance approach.
He said the government also understood the challenges faced by micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in implementing e-Invoicing.
It had therefore introduced the e-Invoice Voluntary Disclosure Programme until Dec 31, 2027, allowing taxpayers to update, review or make corrections without being penalised.
In addition, the government approved an accelerated capital allowance incentive, allowing companies to claim the full allowance within one year for eligible expenditure related to the implementation of e-Invoicing, thereby helping to reduce compliance costs and administrative burdens.
On international tax developments, Amir Hamzah said Malaysia was strengthening its readiness to implement the Global Minimum Tax Framework under the OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework, while stepping up compliance through transfer pricing, information exchange mechanisms and the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF).
He said the measures reflected Malaysia's determination to remain at the forefront of international tax developments while safeguarding the country's revenue base and fiscal sovereignty.
He said a strong tax system is not merely a source of government revenue but also reflects public confidence in government institutions and the willingness of all parties to contribute to national development.
"A strong tax system reflects public confidence in government institutions, as well as the willingness of industry and individuals to contribute towards the well-being of society.
"More importantly, it reflects the government's capacity to use public resources responsibly in national development," he said.
He said recent global developments had shown that countries with strong institutions, robust governance and sustainable public finances were better positioned to weather uncertainty, manage crises and seize new economic opportunities.
